headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default: Dify can read/write files and egress broadly, while cognee handles personal/finance/support data and session memory.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and tool outputs, and cognee processes documents and support data in session memory. If cognee content is routed into Dify without isolation, prompt-like instructions embedded in files can be treated as trusted context. The pairwise pathway is plausible, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are copied into Dify knowledge-base files or prompts without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Dify tools or workflows treat uploaded file text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Restrict Dify ingestion to vetted documents only.
Add a prompt-injection filter before any cognee-to-Dify transfer.
Separate support-data exports from agent prompts.
Use a human review step for any file promoted into Dify knowledge base.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal and finance data, while Dify can read uploaded files, store conversation logs, and send content to model providers and tool APIs. Because Dify has broad network egress and file access, the pair can leak sensitive support data into third-party inference or logs in default workflows.
conditions: IF cognee data is exported into Dify conversations or knowledge-base files, Dify may transmit it to model providers.
IF Dify logging is enabled for workflows handling support or finance data, sensitive content may persist in conversation logs.
mitigations: Disable sensitive-data ingestion into Dify workflows.
Redact personal and finance fields before transfer.
Limit Dify tool/model access to approved providers only.
Turn off or minimize conversation-log retention for sensitive apps.
Use separate tenants/workspaces for support data and general workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and Dify supports multiple instances with shared state via its server datastore. Dify also writes files and executes shell/subprocesses, so overlapping mutable state can conflict if both operate on the same workspace or exported artifacts. The conflict is plausible but not proven to be same-dir by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same exported workspace or knowledge-base directory, file races can occur.
IF Dify workflows mutate shared datastore records derived from cognee outputs, concurrent updates can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Add file-locking around shared artifacts.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same knowledge-base records.
Use immutable export snapshots between agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while Dify is an orchestration platform that can wire tools into agent or workflow actions. If Dify consumes cognee output as authoritative, it can turn an upstream reasoning error into downstream actions or persisted knowledge. That default pathway is dangerous and not self-verifying.
conditions: IF Dify workflows use cognee-generated decisions or workflows as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into actions.
IF Dify tools commit or publish outputs derived from cognee without verification, incorrect content can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any Dify action uses cognee output.
Require citations or source links for cognee-derived claims.
Route high-impact actions through human approval.
Log provenance for every cognee-to-Dify handoff.
Block automatic execution on uncited or low-confidence outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Dify handles conversation logs, model-provider API keys, and tool credentials with broad network egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for regulated data residency, retention, and third-party processing. The pairwise risk is driven by both agents' documented data classes and egress behavior.
conditions: IF personal or finance data from cognee is processed in Dify without a DPA or residency controls, compliance exposure increases.
IF Dify conversation logs retain regulated data longer than cognee's source system, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into Dify.
Configure retention limits for conversation logs.
Restrict Dify to approved regions/providers.
Document a DPA and residency review for regulated data.
Exclude finance and personal data from non-compliant workflows.
